evals.name: new-deployment-from-scratch
evals.prompt: I need to deploy a new Go service called 'checkout' to our dev cluster via ConfigHub. It listens on port 8080 and the image is ghcr.io/acme/checkout:v0.1.0. Help me get it into a Unit with reasonable defaults.
evals.expected_output: Scaffolds literal YAML via kubectl dry-run, stores it in a Unit with --change-desc, then applies set-container-resources-defaults / set-container-probe-defaults / set-pod-container-security-context-defaults (each with --change-desc) to fill in sensible defaults. Does not introduce any template syntax or values file.

evals.name: user-wants-helm-values
evals.prompt: We have this in ConfigHub now but I'd really like to have a values.yaml where I can tweak the replica count and image tag per environment. Can you set that up?
evals.expected_output: Declines politely, explains the config-as-data rule (Units contain literal YAML, no values file split), and proposes the ConfigHub-native alternative: one Space per environment, functions like set-replicas and set-container-image to apply per-env differences, upstream/downstream Unit relationships to clone baseline. Doesn't add a values file.

evals.name: cross-env-parameterization
evals.prompt: Our team wants the same app config in dev, staging, and prod but with different replicas (1, 2, 5) and different image tags. What's the right way to do this in ConfigHub?
evals.expected_output: Recommends Space per env (one per app × environment), upstream baseline with downstream units, applies differences via `cub function do set-replicas` and `set-container-image` per Space with --change-desc. Does not recommend Helm, Kustomize, or a values file.
